text: The contact repository of rwb-comms is served by three operations fixed in RWB-P6-E4039-CON under /api/recovery/comms/v1: GET /parties/{partyId}/contacts, PUT /contacts/{contactKey}/consent and POST /contacts/{contactKey}/verification, with the ten-element contact answer and six error responses.
why: The legacy story copies the notice endpoints, the TSD P6 endpoint inventory stops at API-P6-011 and the Ownership Map P6 REST row holds no contact operation, so the surface must be fixed by the baseline and stated as such.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-039 endpoints table; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18; TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1; Ownership Map v1; Template and Rules v1 R4 naming
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead and the solution architect confirm the three paths and their answers when the rwb-comms OpenAPI document is baselined.
impact: The app story and the panel call the three fixed paths; a consumer built on a legacy notice path would be reading the notice story instead of the contact repository.

text: The contact value, the consent state, the verification, the failed count and the reason of a stop are P1 rwb-source-data rows in rwb_source_data.contact_point_ext, read and written on the rwb-source-data contract; rwb-comms declares no contact table, no contact column and no ACE view, and owns the two contact writes as operations, the consent rule, the decision record and the panel answer.
why: The legacy data table and the FSD A2.18 give contact_point_ext to module P6, while the Ownership Map gives it to P1 and the P6 ownership row names only merge_field, notice and template; DP-01 then forbids a read of another service's table.
read: Ownership Map v1 (contact_point_ext, party_ext, account_ext, valuation_ext under P1 rwb_source_data); P6 context pack ownership rows; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18.2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-05
confirm: The solution architect and the P1 owner confirm that contact_point_ext stays with rwb-source-data and that the consent and verification writes are its operations.
impact: rwb-comms holds no contact copy; a P1 operation that is late or refused leaves the panel with the stale owner state and records no change, and the consent rule is executed on the owner's answer.

text: The three contact operations of rwb-source-data and the rule-version read of rwb-decision are declared as consumed and faked, with the placeholder on their paths, bodies and status codes, and no C row is added to either story of this key.
why: DP-05 sends the contact facts to the rwb-source-data contract and the decision record carries the rule version in force, but no source publishes those operations and the Work Package fixes the Contract dependencies row as empty.
read: Work Package dependency rows of RWB-P6-E4039-APP and RWB-P6-E4039-CON; TSD P1 v3 T3.1; Template and Rules v1 R5.4 and R5.5
confirm: The P1 and P7 contract owners publish the operations before the integration stage, and the rwb-comms tech lead replaces the placeholder in 12.2 and 12.8 with the published names.
impact: The app story builds and passes its tests against the fakes from Day 1; a live run before the P1 operations exist answers 503 and records nothing.

text: The contact repository is served as a panel of the party of a case through the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON, with no screen identifier, field list or masking of its own; SCR-33 Template approval stays with the template stories of the same service.
why: The legacy story names SCR-33 Template approval, which shows a template and its approval states, and no source names a screen for a consent state of a contact point.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-039 screen and states table; FSD P6 Communications v3 Screens list; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-19
confirm: The edge contract owner and the story that owns the case record view confirm the panel and its field list when RWB-PLT-N001-CON is baselined.
impact: No screen of this key calls the service directly; the panel reads the contact answer and offers the two writes through the route.

text: The consent set is the closed GIVEN and WITHDRAWN, taken from the module specification's own acceptance criteria and declared as data with a version; a state changes only when the P1 owner accepts the write and the decision record exists; the service publishes no contact event and a consent change announces nothing.
why: TSD P6 T3.2 holds no consent list and the field catalogue of FSD P6 A2.18 lists notice fields, while the event catalogue holds no contact event, so the vocabulary, the evidence rule and the missing event have to be stated rather than invented.
read: FSD P6 Communications v3 AC-P6-003-01 and AC-EXC-P6-003-01 and A2.18.3.1; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2; Event and Messaging Design v4 sheet Events; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-10
confirm: The business analyst and the compliance and PDPA officer confirm the consent set and the evidence rule before the first release, and the event owner confirms that no contact event is required.
impact: A withdrawn channel leaves the contact plan and the statutory notices keep theirs; a consumer that needs to know of a consent change has no event to subscribe to and must read the contact answer.

text: The contact operations declare capability area Documents with right R for the read and right U for the two writes with the scope applied, and the legacy Litigation C and R rows are kept as the legacy claim of the notice operations.
why: The legacy permission table belongs to the notice endpoints the legacy story copied, and TSD P6 T6.1 gives the primary role of the feature, RW-COMPLY, Documents RU and Litigation R; no source states a Documents C right for a contact write.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-039 permission checks table; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.18.3.3; TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1
confirm: The rwb-access owner and the solution architect confirm the right of a contact write when the authorise contract is baselined.
impact: A role without the Documents right is refused with MSG-P4-002 and a party outside the scope answers 404; the litigation roles keep their notice rights unchanged.
